name: CameraDetailPanel
intent: Floating detail for one camera — its fields plus the violations it caught, as a selectable list.
when: A camera selected on a map needs its record and everything it caught
The violation list is the entry point to individual tickets
A camera preview or live stream sits alongside what the camera caught

chooseOver.because: ObservationDetailPanel is one ticket. CameraDetailPanel is the level above it — the camera and the list of tickets it accounts for, which drills into the ticket panel.

commonMistakes: Giving the camera panel a different width from the ticket panel — the frame visibly jumps when drilling in and back. Both default to 340.
Letting a future stream player size the preview — the 16:9 frame, rounding and clipping belong to the panel. Pass the player as `preview` and let it fill the box.
stubPlan: dataContract: stub — author input fields, slots, rowIdentity
configSchema: stub — enumerate config props from source

lineage.confidence: unset — camera → violation → back flow exercised end-to-end in the browser

usage: Use CameraDetailPanel to structure and organize content within your interface. This component helps create visual hierarchy and consistent spacing throughout your application.
CameraDetailPanel works well for arranging related content, creating responsive layouts, and maintaining visual consistency. Use it to group related elements and establish clear content boundaries.

props.name: violations
props.description: Violations attributed to this camera, newest first. The count badge reads off this list.

props.name: preview
props.description: Replaces the thumbnail entirely — pass a player here once cameras stream live. The 16:9 frame, rounding and clipping stay with the panel, so a player only has to fill its box.

props.name: width
props.description: Panel width in px. Default `340` — matches `ObservationDetailPanel` so the frame never jumps.
